title: The Comet, the Planets, and the Sprite
caption: Comet Leonard, a red sprite, Venus and Saturn over Maunakea
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Soon after sunset on 20 December 2021, a Cloudcam at Gemini North on Maunakea, Hawai‘i, caught several sky phenomena in a single frame. Left of center is Comet Leonard, which was visible to the naked eye, and right of center is a red sprite. Faint red airglow tints the left side, Venus is the brightest feature and Saturn appears at the top.

Red sprites are among the rarest phenomena in the shot. They flash downward from heights of between 50 and 90 kilometers (30–55 miles) toward the tops of the clouds above a thunderstorm, and they are seldom caught on camera. The clear sky and unusual vantage point on Maunakea improve the odds, and another sprite was recorded from the same spot in 2017.

The Gemini North telescope, one of the two halves of the Gemini Observatory run by NSF NOIRLab, sits at around 4200 meters (13,800 feet). That height helps with astronomical observing and also makes the site a fine lookout for light phenomena in the night sky.

understand.summary: A frame from one of the Cloudcams at Gemini North. No exposure details or color mapping are published.
understand.eye: Comet Leonard could be seen with the naked eye, while red sprites are rarely captured even on camera.
